topics.title: Using Past Continuous Tense Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Grammar
topics.content:
ENGLISH STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 2/3/4
PRIMARY 3
THEME - GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY
PREVIOUS LESSON - Expressing Future Action in Negative Primary 1 (Basic 1) - English Structure
TOPIC - USING PAST CONTINUOUS TENSE
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to make correct sentences in the simple future tense.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Sentence strips
2. Course book
3. Other supplementary resources like newspapers or magazines.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
USING PAST CONTINUOUS TENSE
Past continuous tense is used to talk continuous actions of the past.
For example,
1. He was going to school when he fell.
2. He was coming to the house when he met John.
3. I was was listening to radio when she came in.
4. They were playing football after school.
5. Our teacher was teaching in a class.
6. She was washing the clothes when the phone rang.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher explains past continuous tense.
Pupil’s Activities - Listen to teacher’s explanation.
3. Demonstrates the correct use of past continuous tense in sentences.
Pupil’s Activities - Use past continuous tense in sentences.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. identify past continuous tense in sentences, and
2. use past continuous tense in sentences.

topics.title: Present Perfect Using Ed - Ending Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Grammar
topics.content:
ENGLISH STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 5
PRIMARY 3
THEME - GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY
PREVIOUS LESSON -
TOPIC - PRESENT PERFECT USING - ED ENDING
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify present perfect using -ed ending.
2. express correct use of present perfect with -ed ending.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Sentence strips
2. Course book
3. Other supplementary resources like newspapers or magazines.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
PRESENT PERFECT USING - ED AND - EN ENDING
Present perfect tense combines the present tense and the perfect aspect used to express an event that happened in the past that has present consequences. For example,
WORDS PRONUNCIATION - PRESENT PERFECT
work - worked
listen - listened
pray - prayed
lie - lied
place - placed
show - showed
snow - snowed
finish - finished
print - printed
watch - watched, etc.
EXPRESS CORRECT USE OF PRESENT PERFECT with ED - ENDING
Statements:
1. I have cleaned the kitchen.
2. I have washed my clothes.
3. He has finished his classwork
4. She has finished her classwork.
5. She has lived here in Lagos.
6. He has lived here in Lagos.
7. He listened in silence.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher to explain present perfect using both ed - endings.
Pupil’s Activities - Pupils to identify correctly present perfect tense in sentences.
3. Leads pupils in constructing sentences in the present perfect tense.
Pupil’s Activities - Use present perfect tense in sentences.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board with some exercises.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. identify present perfect tense in sentences, and
2. express correct use of present perfect in sentences.

topics.title: Present Prefect with “Since” Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Grammar
topics.content:
ENGLISH STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 8
PRIMARY 3
THEME - GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY
PREVIOUS LESSON - Present Perfect Using Ed - Ending Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Grammar
TOPIC - PRESENT PERFECT WITH “SINCE”
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify present perfect with “since”.
2. express correct use of present perfect with “since”.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Sentence strips
2. Course book
3. Other supplementary resources like newspapers or magazines.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
PRONUNCIATION
Since
For
FOR and SINCE are frequently used with the past perfect tense.
PRESENT PERFECT WITH “SINCE”
SINCE is used with perfect tense.
We use since to talk about a specific point in past time, or a time when the action started. For examples,
Since + a point in past time
- since this morning/afternoon/evening
- since last week/month/year
- since yesterday
- since I was a boy
- since Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday/Thursday/Friday/Saturday/Sunday
- since ____ o’clock
EXPRESS CORRECT USE OF PRESENT PERFECT WITH “SINCE”
1. I have been awake since 8 o’clock.
2. Lunch has been ready since 2 hours ago.
3. He has lived here since 2012.
4. We have taught at this school since last year.
5. They have been at Lagos since last month.
6. He has worked here since 2020.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Explains the correct use of present perfect with “since” and “for”.
Pupil’s Activities - Correctly use present perfect with “since”, following teacher’s examples.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board with some exercises.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Present Prefect with “For” Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Grammar
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. identify present perfect with “since”.
2. use “since” in sentence construction.
WORKBOOK
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
As stated in week 9.

topics.title: Present Prefect with “For” Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Structure
topics.content:
ENGLISH STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 9
PRIMARY 3
THEME - STRUCTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Present Prefect with “Since” Primary 3 (Basic 3) - English Grammar
TOPIC - PRESENT PERFECT WITH “FOR”
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify present perfect with “for”.
3. express correct use of present perfect with “for”.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Sentence strips
2. Course book
3. Other supplementary resources like newspapers or magazines.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
PRONUNCIATION
since
for
FOR and SINCE are frequently used with the past perfect tense.
PRESENT PERFECT WITH “FOR”
FOR is used with the simple past. We use for to talk about a period of time. For examples,
For + a period of past time
- for ten days
- for a month
- for a month
- for hours
- for twelve hours
- for two years
EXPRESS CORRECT USE OF PRESENT PERFECT WITH “FOR”
1. I have been sick for two days.
2. Mum has been in the market for two hours.
3. He has lived here for nine years.
4. They have been at home for two week.
5. We have taught at this school for a week.
6. She have worked here for five years.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Explains the correct use of present perfect with “for”.
Pupil’s Activities - Correctly use present perfect with “for”, following teacher’s examples.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board with some exercises.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. identify present perfect with “since” and “for”, and
2. use “since” and “for” in sentence construction.
WORKBOOK
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
1. I have lived in Lagos ___________ ten years.
A. since
B. for
2. I have played football ___________ I was a child.
A. since
B. for
3. He hasn’t had a day off ___________ three weeks.
A. since
B. for
4. I’ve lost so much flexibility ___________ I injured my hand.
A. since
B. for
5. They have all improved in attitude ___________ the manager talked to them.
A. since
B. for
6. Conflicts have been happening ___________ centuries, it won’t ever change.
A. since
B. for
7. I haven’t been on holiday ___________ ages.
A. since
B. for
8. I haven’t eaten that much ___________ Easter.
A. since
B. for
9. They haven’t been on holiday ___________ last month.
A. since
B. for
10. He hasn’t seen his bag ___________ morning, I think he lost it.
A. since
B. for

topics.title: Vocabulary Building (Teaching of New Words) Primary 3 (Basic 3) English Studies
topics.content:
ENGLISH STUDIES
FIRST TERM
SECOND TERM
THIRD TERM
WEEK 1 2 3…..
PRIMARY 3
TOPIC: NEW WORDS
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identify new words and pronounce them correctly.
2. recognize new words meaning.
3. demonstrate the meaning of the new words.
4. use the new words in sentences.
ENTRY BEHAVIOR
Most of the pupils can spell and pronounce the new words correctly.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of course book, chart containing new words and dictionary.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Materials
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
NEW WORDS AND SPELLING

2.
3.
NEW WORDS AND MEANING
1.
2.
3.
MAKING SIMPLE SENTENCE WITH THE SELECTED NEW WORDS
1.
2.
3.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays chart showing selected new words.
3. Lets the pupils spell each word on the chart correctly.
Pupil’s Activities - Spell each of the word on the chart correctly.
4. Reads and let the pupils in groups or pairs repeat after you.
5. Lets the find the new words in the passage.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify the new words in the passage.
6. Organizes the pupils in groups or pair to study and deduce the contextual meaning of the unfamiliar words.
Pupil’s Activities - Deduce the contextual meaning of the unfamiliar words.
7. In groups or pairs, guide the pupils to find the meaning of the new words in the dictionary.
Pupil’s Activities - Find the meaning of the new words in the dictionary.
8. Guides pupils to pronounce the new words by breaking them into sound.
Pupil’s Activities - Follow the teacher’s guide to break new words into sound and pronounce correctly.
9. Lets the pupils use the new words in sentences.
10. Writes the words and their meanings on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Write and explain the meaning of the new words.
11. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the summary of the lesson.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
LESSON EVALUATION/ASSIGNMENT
Ask pupils to -
1. identify new words and pronounce them correctly.
2. recognize new words meaning.
3. demonstrate the meaning of the new words.
4. use the new words in sentences.
